problem: Clause 2.6.5 holds a second written-answer requirement besides the one the item excepts: the full report on an enquiry ballot "shall" "d) include the observations of the secretariat of the committee on each of the comments submitted." That is a written answer to every enquiry comment, including those behind negative votes, and "observation" is not among the searched terms. No other listed clause adds one: 2.6.4 has a group "at a meeting, address any comments received", 2.7.5 records final-draft comments as "noted for future consideration", and 2.7.7 refers a failed final draft back "for reconsideration".
fix: Write "Apart from 2.6.5's required responses and observations on all comments received, no ISO/IEC Directives Part 1 clause listed here requires a written answer to a working group or ballot objection" and add observation to the searched terms. l:iso-comment-answers already states both requirements.

problem: SD-4 ("Proposals and papers") limits this discretion in time: "At early discussion phases, subgroup chairs have discretion to allow limited exploration of alternatives to an active proposal to decide whether a second paper is warranted, or to discuss broader prerequisite topics that are exposed by a paper under discussion." The same section says "we do not significantly delay progress on concrete proposals in order to wait for alternative proposals we might get in the future." The lemma gives the move to any chair at any stage.
fix: "and allow early, limited exploration of alternatives" (the sentence stays at 27 words). l:checks-alternatives has the same gap.

problem: Step 6 of SD-4's "How to report a potential technical concern, at any level of severity" reads "File the issue or write the paper, or otherwise make sure such a follow-up happens." The reporter can meet it by making sure someone else files or writes, so "SD-4 asks whoever raises a concern to file an issue or write a paper" asks more than the step does.
fix: "SD-4 asks whoever raises a concern to see an issue filed or a paper written, and outside the protected records only writing keeps an objection's argument after its hearers leave." (30 words)

problem: The same step 6: "File the issue or write the paper, or otherwise make sure such a follow-up happens. Ensure the feature's designers (proposal authors) are aware of the follow-up issue or paper." The lemma drops the third option.
fix: "SD-4 asks whoever reports a concern to see an issue filed or a paper written, and to make sure the feature's designers know of it."

problem: SD-4 ("Consensus") conditions its description on a hearing: "The minority, once they have had opportunity to be heard, cannot just say “we still object so you can't proceed” and refuse to accept the consensus of the majority to pursue a different direction." The proposition rightly says "whether or not anyone answered it" but drops "once they have had opportunity to be heard", so it reaches an objector who was never heard, whom the same section protects: "The majority cannot just say “we have enough votes” and refuse to listen to the concerns of the minority."
fix: "SD-4 describes an objector who, once heard, keeps objecting after a consensus call without new information or allowed escalation as not accepting a group decision, answered or not." (28 words)

problem: ISO 1.7: "Nevertheless, all National Bodies, irrespective of their status within a committee, have the right to vote on enquiry drafts (see 2.6) and on final draft International Standards (see 2.7)." Under d:national-body a national body is an SC22 P-member, so ISO member bodies that are not SC22 P-members also cast enquiry and final ballot votes, and "national bodies cast those in the ballots on its drafts" leaves them out.
fix: "Apart from guests, whose choices the proof takes as given, participants cast the votes in WG21's polls and ISO member bodies cast those in the ballots on its drafts." (29 words) p:users-out and inf:thm-no-user-vote, which name national bodies as users' only ballot channel, need the same widening.

problem: The extract supports "plenary approves the changes in that form" in SD-4's "Working draft handling": "To approve the change, instead of a poll to apply a paper to the working draft, we have a poll to approve the changes in the form already applied to the new working draft paper." But f:in-situ, the only cited Fact for this case, quotes the lead sentence and the editing-committee bullet and leaves this one out, so no cited Fact states it.
fix: Add that sentence to f:in-situ's quotation, between the two it already quotes.

problem: SD-4 ("Technical Specifications (TS) and White Papers") says "A TS goes through similar ISO balloting as an IS" and is "formally balloted with a round of formal review comments collated by ISO that must be formally responded to with a Disposition of Comments paper". Unscoped, "ISO requires ... no other written answer to an objection" contradicts that account; its basis, f:iso-no-answer, covers only the clauses it lists, and none of them mentions a Disposition of Comments.
fix: "ISO requires responses to all comments on an enquiry ballot, with written observations on each, and its quoted clauses require no other written answer to an objection." (27 words)

problem: INCITS 3.9.2 scopes the exception: "Note: On TCs, TGs, and SGs, the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) is allowed a maximum of four votes from separate and unrelated entities", while 3.9.2.1 allows "only one voting membership for separate government subdivision or agency." "The Defense Department up to four" with no scope extends the exception to every INCITS vote, the Executive Board's included.
fix: "In the United States, INCITS caps each organization's votes, denies a vote to consultants a voting member funds, and binds delegates to official positions," leaving the Defense Department exception to l:incits-votes.

problem: The same note: "On TCs, TGs, and SGs, the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) is allowed a maximum of four votes from separate and unrelated entities". "On technical committees" leaves out TGs and SGs, so the lemma implies one Defense Department vote there.
fix: "INCITS gives each organization one voting membership, the Defense Department up to four on TCs, TGs, and SGs, and on its Executive Board counts a controlled entity with its controller." (30 words)

problem: ISO 6.5: "When an appeal is against a decision relating to work in progress, the work shall be continued up to and including the approval stage (see 2.7)." "Continuing up to approval" can be read as stopping before the approval stage, which the clause includes.
fix: "An appeal leaves work on a draft continuing through the approval stage, and against a draft it is eligible only over principle or harm to ISO's or IEC's reputation." (29 words)

problem: ISO 2.6.5's trigger reads "If, within eight weeks from the date of dispatch, two or more P-members disagree with the decision of the Chair, the draft shall be discussed at a meeting (see Clause 5)." But 2.6.4 already has "an appropriate group of the committee, which would typically be the working group to which the project is assigned" meet to "address any comments received and prepare, as needed, a revised version", so a draft is discussed at a meeting without that trigger. The inference states the trigger as needed for any discussion.
fix: "Having a draft discussed at a meeting over the SC22 chair's decision needs at least one other P-member to disagree with it within eight weeks of the report's dispatch." (29 words)

problem: As for m:moves-chair, SD-4 ("Proposals and papers") grants the discretion only at early phases: "At early discussion phases, subgroup chairs have discretion to allow limited exploration of alternatives to an active proposal". Listed as a check, "Chairs may allow limited exploration of alternatives" reads as available at any stage.
fix: "Chairs may allow early, limited exploration of alternatives, and SD-4 encourages side-by-side polls and asks a good paper for alternatives considered, design principles, and motivating examples from today's code." (29 words)

problem: ISO 2.5.7's steps are that the leadership "shall first assess whether the opposition can be considered a “sustained opposition”", if not "will register the opposition (i.e. in the report/minutes, records, etc.) and continue to lead the work on the document", and if so "shall try and resolve it in good faith." No step records an answer. "ISO's steps for assessing, registering, and addressing a sustained opposition, with a recorded answer" can be read as putting a recorded answer among ISO's steps.
fix: "If SD-4 adopted ISO's steps for assessing, registering, and addressing a sustained opposition and added a recorded answer, it would state a step for assessing and registering one." (28 words)

problem: ISO 0.7: "National Bodies need to recognize that substantial comments tabled at meetings are counter-productive". The clause says meetings, not committee meetings. In the Directives "committee" means TCs, SCs, PCs, and SyCs (0.7 e), and under d:national-body "the committee" is SC22, so "committee meetings" excludes the WG21 meetings to which the inference then applies the warning.
fix: Drop "committee": "ISO tells national bodies that substantial comments tabled at meetings are counter-productive, which limits how far cheaper positions turn into substantial comments tabled during a meeting."

problem: second sentence, 104 words: "For this proof, a participant values adoption of the proposals they support, ... and their own time and money."
fix: Keep the first sentence and add "For this proof, each values what the items below name." Then one child Axiom per player, one sentence each: "A participant values adoption of the proposals they support, their standing, keeping any chair or convenor post they hold, their time and money, and a good result for users." "A participant with a sponsor also values the sponsor's interests." "A sponsor values its interests, which can depend on particular features of a design." "A national body values the outcomes its national position supports, the interests concerned at its national level where it has no position yet, and its members' time." "A user values the features they use or would use, how well those features work, and their own time and money."

problem: 31 words: "each with the features approved by its feature cutoff"
fix: WG21 plans a new edition of the C++ standard every three years, with the features approved by its feature cutoff, and ISO publishes each edition once national bodies approve it.

problem: first sentence, 31 words: "Neither SD-4 nor any ISO/IEC Directives Part 1 clause listed here asks an author to state who pays their costs or what interests they or a sponsor have in a proposal."
fix: Neither SD-4 nor any listed ISO/IEC Directives Part 1 clause asks an author to state who pays their costs or what interests they or a sponsor have in a proposal.

problem: "† marks a Pareto-optimal cell." (jargon a reader outside the committee does not know, and the proof never defines it)
fix: † marks a cell that no other cell ranks higher for one regular without ranking lower for the other.

problem: "Whoever ISO's leadership is for a working group," (the claim about SD-4's steps holds without it)
fix: SD-4's steps for an objection include the 2:1 norm, Against voters' reasons on request, escalation, and plenary's 3-way poll and national-position question.

problem: "an unwritten reason survives only in the memory of those who heard it"
fix: A proposal's case lasts for decades in its required paper, while an unwritten reason is kept only in the memory of those who heard it.

problem: "an objection's argument survives outside the protected records only in writing"
fix: Once no one who heard it can be asked, an objection's argument is kept outside the protected records only in writing.

problem: "Participants learn how the committee applies them partly, and some only, by attending" (hard to parse)
fix: Other things equal, whoever knows more of how the committee applies them, some of it learned only by attending, has the better chance of adoption, whatever their design skill.

problem: "Three things hold at once for an objector who arrives after a design has been adopted." (opens with no claim, and "its case" has no clear owner)
fix: An objector who arrives after a design is adopted needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, against a reversal cost that grows as more is built. The record keeps the design's case, but unwritten objections only in memory.

problem: "objections no one wrote down survive only with those who heard them"
fix: The design's case lasts in its paper, while objections no one wrote down are kept only by those who heard them.

problem: "† marks a Pareto-optimal cell." (jargon a reader outside the committee does not know, and the proof never defines it)
fix: † marks a cell that no other cell ranks higher for one group without ranking lower for the other.

problem: "seldom turns on one user's effort"
fix: No user votes, and taking part costs the participant or their sponsor, while a better design's gain is spread across all users and seldom depends on one user's effort.

problem: "Users' interests reach decisions only through"
fix: Users' interests affect decisions only through what participants themselves value, papers a participant presents, TS feedback, and national bodies, which form positions only where that is worth their members' time.

problem: the condition "a study group chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost them", which this lemma states and l:sg-call, inf:sg-call-default, l:sg-side-by-side, and l:sg-other-moves each repeat
fix: Keep the condition in this lemma and write "such a chair" in each child, for example: "When several designs compete, such a chair does best polling them side by side."

problem: the condition "a design room chair whose stake is worth less than what departing can cost", which this lemma states and l:dchair-call, l:dchair-side-by-side, and l:dchair-other-moves each repeat
fix: Keep the condition in this lemma and write "such a chair" in each child, for example: "For every count after discussion, such a chair ranks first the call the 2:1 norm gives."

problem: "the needs that reach a vote are those participants and their sponsors know"
fix: No user votes, and the needs put to a vote are those participants and their sponsors know, which need not match those of users at large.

problem: "unwritten objections survive only in memory"
fix: Removing an adopted design needs a paper or ballot comment meeting the 2:1 norm, reversal costs more for every decision built on it, and unwritten objections remain only in memory.

problem: "the needs that reach a vote"
fix: No user votes, and the needs put to a vote are those participants and their sponsors know, which need not match those of users at large.

problem: "users' interests reach decisions only through"
fix: No user votes, and users' interests affect decisions only through what participants value, papers a participant presents, TS feedback, and national bodies.

problem: "values the sponsor's interests, so they weigh the proposal's adoption as a gain" (neither cited item makes adoption one of a sponsor's interests; only the parent's condition does)
fix: A participant whose costs the sponsor pays values the sponsor's interests, here including the proposal's adoption, so they weigh that adoption as a gain against any doubt about it.

problem: "large designs mostly adopted in one paper" (the same sentence says "large proposals", the term proof-terms assigns)
fix: The model predicts that large proposals tend to arrive as sequences of papers, each building on adopted parts, and large proposals mostly adopted in one paper would count against it.

problem: "Large designs mostly adopted in one paper"
fix: Large proposals mostly adopted in one paper would count against the prediction.

problem: "whether a large design arrived in one paper or in parts"
fix: Every significant proposal requires a paper and a published paper stays available, so the mailings show whether a large proposal arrived in one paper or in parts.

problem: "If large designs are easier to review in parts"
fix: If large proposals are easier to review in parts, that ease would also yield sequences of papers.

problem: "small first papers" ("small" here means scope, but the chapter also uses the defined term small proposal)
fix: For design-bound authors, the model predicts first papers of small scope that leave out the later parts of a design extended part by part; the mailings are the evidence.

problem: "would also yield small first papers"
fix: The lower risk of small first steps would also yield first papers of small scope.

problem: "even with no hurdle to removing them"
fix: If adopted designs rarely need removal, removals would be rare even if the 2:1 norm and the reversal cost did not apply to removing them.

problem: "so the hurdle shows in such failures"
fix: Under the 2:1 norm, a removal poll with more Favor than Against votes but not twice as many fails, so such failures show the norm's effect on removal.

problem: "the record would show whether an objection was answered" (the premise already requires the answer in the record)
fix: If the rules required the record to hold a written answer to each objection, every objection would be in writing whatever the paper says.

problem: "a deadlock lasting that long would end by that procedure" (true by the premise)
fix: If the rules set a decision procedure for deadlocks lasting a set number of meetings, no group would bear the cost of holding through a deadlock for longer.

problem: "it would state a step for assessing and registering one" (true by the premise)
fix: If SD-4 adopted ISO's steps for assessing, registering, and addressing a sustained opposition, with a recorded answer, a declared opposition left unresolved would be registered in writing.

problem: "limits how far cheaper positions turn into substantial comments"
fix: ISO tells national bodies that substantial comments tabled at committee meetings are counter-productive, which limits how many cheaper positions become substantial comments tabled during a meeting.

problem: "so fewer still makes plenary opposition holding them seldom" (hard to parse)
fix: In the settled pattern national bodies already state positions on few proposals, so with fewer still, plenary seldom meets opposition holding them.

problem: f:minority-accept describes as not accepting a group decision a heard minority that says "we still object so you can't proceed" and refuses to accept the consensus, not every objector who keeps objecting. An objector who goes on disagreeing while accepting the decision falls outside the quoted text.
fix: Narrow the subject to "an objector who, once heard, keeps insisting after a consensus call that the work cannot proceed, without new information or allowed escalation".

problem: Its children l:call-above and l:call-below, and the t:chair-call caption, establish the ranking only for a design room chair, yet p:chair-default concludes it for any chair, and inf:sg-call-default relies on it for study group chairs.
fix: Write "a chair" for "a design room chair" in l:call-above and the t:chair-call caption, since their bases f:two-to-one and d:follows-norm cover every subgroup poll.

problem: "and no other written answer to an objection" claims more than f:iso-no-answer, which covers only the clauses it lists. f:ts-disposition says comments on a TS ballot "must be formally responded to with a Disposition of Comments paper", which the sibling l:ts-comment-answers relies on.
fix: Narrow it to "and no other clause the proof quotes requires a written answer to an objection".

problem: It says only the No counts against approval, but its basis inf:no-counts-against and l:ballot-rules count a No only when it carries technical comments, and a No without them ties with abstaining. Nothing in the table's case says this body's No carries technical comments.
fix: State once in the t:nb-ballot caption that a No in either column carries comments of a technical nature, as f:no-conditional-yes requires on a final draft.

problem: Ranking abstaining strictly above No needs this body's No to carry technical comments, since inf:no-counts-against counts only such a No, and the case never says its comments are technical.
fix: The same single caption statement in t:nb-ballot fixes this, so no separate change is needed.

problem: "which is all that author's gain depends on" claims more than d:design-bound, which says the author's gain depends on keeping particular features fixed but, unlike d:result-seeking, never says it depends on nothing else. A sponsor whose interests also gain from early reach to users is not excluded.
fix: Replace the clause with "the value d:design-bound names", so that d:does-better, which l:bound-vehicle already cites, holds the author's other values equal.

problem: No cited item says a direction poll speeds the polls after it: d:polls defines the poll and f:design-forward describes forwarding, but neither makes a direction poll a step before forwarding.
fix: Add a cited premise that an early poll brings the author the room's direction sooner, from f:negative-welcome (polls give "meaningful and actionable feedback") and f:direction-implement (directed changes come "typically for subsequent revisions of the proposal to be considered at the next meeting").

problem: "A sponsor pays for participants where the decisions it values are made" drops the condition l:settled-sponsor proves, "while what they bring it is worth their cost", and is false without it for a sponsor whose participants are not worth what they cost.
fix: Add "while what they bring it is worth their cost" to that sentence.

problem: It has each choice the Theorem leaves open "made the way that does best for its player given the others' choices" and concludes a settled pattern, but no cited item shows that such mutually best choices exist together. The open choices of different players can depend on one another, so their joint existence is an assumption.
fix: Either add, as a stated assumption cited here, that the open choices admit a set of mutual best responses, or narrow the Theorem to "every settled pattern includes these choices", which the whatever-the-others-choose lemmas already prove.

problem: "whether to study a paper is a choice each participant makes the way that does best for them" covers non-regular participants and guests, whose choices m:players takes as given, so "that review goes undone" goes beyond what l:thm-pattern settles.
fix: Narrow the subject to the players, "a choice each player makes the way that does best for them, so no player does that review", and match the Theorem's sentence to it.

problem: "SD-4 never uses the word trade-off" is not supplied by f:no-drawbacks-asked, which says only that the searched terms, trade-off among them, occur in limited contexts, not that the word is absent from SD-4.
fix: Add that absence to f:no-drawbacks-asked's search result and cite it, or else cut the clause, which l:thm-disclosure does not use.

problem: "which movers and stayers polled together share" assumes movers learn after the move only what stayers learn, but no cited item rules out technical learning from the new sponsor's colleagues, which would also turn movers' votes only after the move.
fix: State as a condition of the test that a move brings the mover no technical learning the stayers lack, or weaken "favor the model" to "fit the model and also views learned at the new sponsor".

problem: It predicts fewer votes as revisions grow longer but drops the condition its basis inf:al-study keeps, that participants' stakes are unchanged, though stakes can rise as a proposal moves from direction polls to forwarding polls.
fix: State once in c:pred-abstention-length that the comparison is among polls of the same form, with participants' stakes in the proposal held fixed.

problem: ax:review-cost says added length adds review time, so stating what later parts need costs reviewers something, and "costs reviewers little" supports at most "little reason" to omit it, not "no reason".
fix: Write "gives little reason to omit it" here and "gives an author little reason" in inf:pa-tell-apart.

problem: "Reflection made before submission" limits the other explanation to reflection before submission, which inf:sf-reflection does not, and a sponsor that stops paying after reassessing the proposal would raise stops after the loss under reflection too.
fix: Narrow the test to sponsor losses unrelated to the proposal, such as a sponsor ending all its WG21 participation, and drop the limit to reflection before submission.

problem: Its basis gives only that a national body forms a position where that is worth its members' time and that a ballot vote needs none, which does not make positions few rather than many. So positions on most proposals would not count against what the cited items predict.
fix: Predict instead fewer positions where forming one costs more, which inf:nb-tell-apart already tests, and carry the change into c:pred-nb-positions and inf:nl-fewer, which rely on "few".

problem: "agreement predicts no such difference" assumes bodies whose experts attend in person agree with proposals as often as others, but f:in-person-expected, which it cites, says bodies send experts in person "if they want to affect the direction of the standard". Under the agreement explanation those bodies could disagree more often and so state more positions.
fix: Narrow the comparison to one body's positions across meetings with and without its experts present in person, which holds the body itself fixed.

problem: "Close study worth less to any one participant than its cost goes undone" claims more than p:review-shortfall, which says only that no participant does better doing it, and participants whose choices m:players takes as given may still do it.
fix: Write "is study no participant does better doing", which still supports "can lack study".

problem: "the cost left to an author of accepting one would be the risk" treats the two costs p:prefer-is names as the only ones, but f:ts-disposition also lists a TS's formal ballot, Disposition of Comments, and ISO editing.
fix: Write "the cost p:prefer-is names that would remain is the risk", which still supports the falling cost c:lever-ts-path states.

problem: The proof takes the convenor's appointments as given, so no choice inside the settled pattern removes a chair who departs from the 2:1 norm. Every chair result (p:chair-default, l:settled-sg-chair, l:settled-design-chair) then rests on ax:post-risk alone, and "taken as given" can be read as appointments that do not respond to a chair's calls, which would leave departing free.
fix: State once, here, that taking the appointments as given leaves the convenor free to replace a chair (f:chairs-appointed), that the proof does not model when the convenor does so, and that the chair results rest on ax:post-risk.

problem: The list leaves out moves the rules give a regular: posting a serious objection on the committee email lists (f:escalate-deadline), telling the chairs and authors of a concern and filing an issue (f:report-early, f:report-followup), and commenting on or objecting to minutes (f:minutes-objections). l:regular-other-moves and inf:thm-other-moves claim the named votes do best whatever other moves a regular takes, so moves missing here are never checked.
fix: Add these moves and their facts to m:moves-regular, and add them to inf:regular-alongside as moves that go with any vote.

problem: "One Against vote changes the result only when the count is one or two votes above the 2:1 threshold" counts only the vote's arithmetic. Under f:two-to-one the norm applies "after discussion of the concerns of those voting against and possibly a re-poll", so an Against vote also secures a hearing for the voter's concerns before any re-poll, and what others learn there can change their votes (ax:attention) far from the threshold. l:vote-count and the chapter 3 summary use the same words, and l:settled-regular rests on them.
fix: Write "One Against vote changes whether the count meets the norm only when the count is one or two votes above the 2:1 threshold, and through the discussion of its concerns before any re-poll it can also change other votes or the design," citing ax:attention, and use the same words in l:vote-count.

problem: SD-4 describes as not accepting group decisions a minority that, once heard, says "we still object so you can't proceed" and refuses to accept the majority's consensus (f:minority-accept). It does not say this of everyone who keeps objecting: a later paper proposing a change is an ordinary proposal, and SD-4 only encourages people not to rehash decisions without new information (f:pre-merge). The broader subject feeds l:settled-regular and the Theorem's claim that objections count only in fixed forms.
fix: Narrow the subject: "SD-4 describes an objector who, after being heard, insists that the majority cannot proceed, without new information or allowed escalation, as not accepting a group decision, whether or not anyone answered the objection."

problem: The list of channels leaves out the issues lists, which SD-4 names beside papers when it asks whoever reports a concern to "File the issue or write the paper" (f:report-followup). An issue also puts a concern in writing outside the password-protected materials, so "only a paper" is false for a concern an issue can hold, and inf:objector-paper repeats the claim.
fix: Add issues lists and keep the claim for design objections: "only a paper puts a design objection's argument outside the password-protected materials ..., since SD-4 requires a paper for every design change and sends minor wording issues to the issues lists (f:no-paper)."

problem: SD-4 says all meetings are minuted, "This includes telecons as well as in-person meetings" (f:minutes), and a study group that meets by telecon between meetings meets alongside no other room. Its voters there are those for whom its topic is worth the time, not those for whom it outweighs a parallel room, so the selection p:sg-sponsor builds on holds only for sessions held alongside other rooms.
fix: Scope the second sentence: "So when a study group meets alongside other rooms, its voters are those for whom its topic outweighs them," citing f:minutes for telecons.

problem: The chair may take any polls they choose (f:chair-polls), including SD-4's approval polls, where not raising a hand for an alternative marks the voter as opposed to it, and polls that ask voters to choose between two designs. When the rival is another colleague's, backing the supported design is attributable opposition to the colleague's, so under ax:support it can cost standing with that colleague. "Favor does best ... whatever the others choose" here, and "Favor risks nothing with the colleague" in the Theorem, fail in exactly the side-by-side polls the proof has chairs take.
fix: State the scope once: "On a poll of one colleague's proposal, ...", and add to l:settled-regular that in a poll choosing between two colleagues' designs, a vote for one counts as a vote Against the other under ax:support.

problem: "the call that norm gives: a design meeting it, or none when none does" leaves the call open when more than one design meets the 2:1 norm, which side-by-side polls allow since a participant can vote Favor on several. Choosing among designs that all meet the norm departs from nothing, so the chair's stake can decide it at no risk to their post, and l:settled-sg-chair's "sending on a design that meets the 2:1 norm" does not say which.
fix: Add: "When more than one design meets the norm, SD-4 polls them to see which has most consensus (f:multiple-polls), and the proof leaves the chair's choice among them open," and name that choice among those the Theorem leaves open.

problem: "For every count after discussion" includes counts at which Neutral votes are a majority of those voting, for which d:follows-norm defines no call and SD-4 says only that this "can be concerning" (f:two-to-one). There the norm gives no call to rank first, so the lemma is unsupported at those counts, and the same gap opens when more than one rival meets the norm. The Theorem's "Chairs follow the 2:1 norm" then leaves both cases unstated.
fix: Scope the first sentence: "For every count after discussion with Neutral votes short of a majority, ...", and list the call at a Neutral majority, and the choice among rivals that all meet the norm, among the choices the Theorem leaves open.

problem: At the feature cutoff a one-meeting delay costs the proposal an edition, and SD-4's own text weighs against that: "we do not significantly delay progress on concrete proposals in order to wait for alternative proposals we might get in the future" (f:no-wait-alternatives). The proof quotes the sentence but applies it neither here nor in inf:dchair-delay, which treats the delay as the chair's free choice.
fix: Add "though SD-4 says it does not significantly delay concrete proposals to wait for alternatives," citing f:no-wait-alternatives, here and in inf:dchair-delay.

problem: A chair's plenary summary is spoken, and any record of it is in the meeting wiki, which SD-4 password-protects and lets be quoted publicly only for poll questions, numeric results, and words a person consents to have attributed (f:protected), or in minutes the proof does not show to be public. The proof names no public record of the summaries, so the data meant to tell the two explanations apart may not be usable.
fix: State that using the summaries needs the chair's prior consent or access to protected records, citing f:protected, as inf:sa-consent does for named votes.

problem: Only objections someone raises at plenary get a summary, and an objector is likelier to raise one there when they think it went unanswered. That selection leans the sample toward unanswered objections whatever the truth, so a high share of them does not favor the model over answers given in discussion.
fix: Compare the share shown unanswered among omitted objections with the same share among objections the paper does state, both raised at plenary, so that the selection applies to both.

problem: Under that rule a supporter's Favor vote would also bear the reasons cost, while l:vote-count shows one vote seldom changes the result. A supporter whose vote would not change the result would then also do better not voting, so the model predicts fewer Favor votes on supported proposals as well, which changes how many proposals meet the norm.
fix: Add to the prediction "and fewer Favor votes from supporters whose vote seldom changes the result," resting on l:vote-count and inf:ra-cost.

problem: SD-4 names a step for checking a design in the context of the whole standard: merging a TS or white paper early "to permit better 'integration testing' as we refine it further in the full context of the IS, and permit other parts of the standard to adapt to the new feature" (f:early-merge), which l:checks-deadlock already counts as a check. So "No SD-4 step checks whether the designs work together" here, and the same words in inf:thm-fit and the Theorem, need that exception.
fix: Write "Apart from merging a TS or white paper early for integration testing, no SD-4 step checks whether designs adopted in separate papers work together," citing f:early-merge.

problem: d:participant excludes guests a convenor invites, and d:user counts as a user any person who writes C++ and "does not participate". ISO invites a guest "to participate" (f:guests), but the proof never says whether a guest participates in d:user's sense. If not, a guest who writes C++ is a user who votes in the room, against "no user votes" here, in p:users-out, and in the Theorem.
fix: State once, in d:user or here, that a guest invited under f:guests participates and so is not a user.

problem: The list leaves out convenor moves the quoted rules give: seeing that meeting outcomes are documented and addressing comments on the minutes (f:minutes-objections), and reviewing participation to report persistently inactive experts (f:inactive-experts). The first shapes what the record keeps, and l:convenor-given and inf:thm-other-moves claim the convenor's named choice does best whatever other moves the convenor takes.
fix: Add both moves and their facts here, and show in l:convenor-given that they go with following SD-4's plenary procedure, or list them among the choices the Theorem leaves open.

problem: ISO 5.4, the clause f:late-documents quotes, goes on: "Ad hoc groups are exempt from the deadline requirements set out in Table 3" and "Successive meetings operating from the same agenda (i.e. comments resolution on the same document) are also exempt from these deadline requirements." So at ballot comment resolution a late document needs no agreement from all present, which limits the fixed times this lemma and the Theorem describe for ballot-stage objections.
fix: Add a Fact quoting both sentences and write "and, outside ad hoc groups and ballot comment resolution, ISO requires every participant present to agree before a decision on matters with late documents."

problem: SD-4 says "Any technical changes made during ballot comment resolution have one goal: to improve consensus," and explains its near-unanimity rule after a final ballot by the need for "strong confidence that the design change is not reducing the existing consensus" among national bodies not present. A removal in answer to a ballot comment is judged by that test as well as by the room's 2:1 count, and the proof quotes neither sentence.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the "one goal: to improve consensus" sentence and write "a removal by paper needs the 2:1 norm in a design room, and one in answer to a ballot comment is also judged, SD-4 says, by whether it improves consensus."

problem: "SD-4 gives no weight to objections not escalated in time" states as an outcome what SD-4 states as guidance: such objections "should not be given weight in plenary" (f:plenary-weight), while plenary's consensus is "as determined by the Convener" (f:plenary-owns). l:settled-convenor needs the line between what SD-4 fixes and what it leaves to the convenor drawn exactly.
fix: Write "SD-4 says objections not escalated in time should get no weight there," as l:plenary-late-weight does.

problem: SD-4's sentence on weight sits in its section on escalating a serious "cannot live with" objection and speaks of objections "raised or re-raised in plenary". It does not say that a vote cast in the 3-way poll SD-4's plenary procedure prescribes is such an objection. Equating every unescalated plenary Against vote with one is a reading, and l:convenor-weightless, l:settled-convenor, and the Theorem's claim that SD-4 has the convenor declare consensus rest on it; under the other reading SD-4 leaves the call to the convenor whenever anyone votes Against.
fix: Add the reading as a stated premise once: "This proof reads a plenary Against vote not backed by timely escalation as an objection raised in plenary, which SD-4 says should not be given weight," and cite it in l:convenor-weightless.

problem: "and no other written answer to an objection" reaches further than f:iso-no-answer, which covers only "a working group or ballot objection". An appeal is an objection to a decision, and the searched clauses have the parent committee "consider and decide on the appeal" (6.2.2) and the technical management board "address the appeal at its next meeting" (6.3.3). p:written-answer's "No rule requires a written answer to an objection beyond ..." has the same reach.
fix: Narrow both to "a working group or ballot objection", and leave appeals to inf:record-appeal.

problem: ISO says "Every attempt shall be made to resolve negative votes" (quoted in f:respond-comments) and refers a failed final draft back "for reconsideration in light of the technical reasons submitted in support of the negative votes" (f:failed-fdis). Under ISO's text, comments sent with a No get treatment that comments sent with a Yes do not, so the case the table, p:credible-threat, and l:settled-nb rest on, a body whose comments fare the same under any vote, rests on SD-4's statement against ISO's.
fix: State the case as a premise once: "The table's case is a body that expects ISO's attempts to resolve negative votes to add nothing to the consideration SD-4 says WG21 gives all comments," citing f:respond-comments and f:no-means-no.

problem: "negative votes without technical comments go uncounted" leaves out ISO's check on that discount: when a negative vote's comments are not clearly technical, the Secretary/Committee Manager "shall contact the National Body within two weeks of the ballot closure", and without agreement "the matter is escalated to the technical management board" (2.6.2, 2.7.2).
fix: Add a Fact quoting that passage and write "negative votes whose comments are found not technical, after ISO's contact with the body and any escalation, go uncounted."

problem: The lemma says SD-4 "asks for respect, good faith, and no collusion", but ISO 0.7, a clause chapter 1 quotes, says "Individuals participating in ISO and IEC activities must comply with the mandatory ISO Code of Ethics and Conduct [5] and the IEC Code of conduct [6] for technical work." The conduct items quoted from SD-4's slide are duties, not requests, and they bear on the sponsor and objector results the Theorem sets against the checks.
fix: Add a Fact quoting 0.7 f) and write "SD-4 displays, and ISO makes mandatory, the Code's calls for respect, good faith, and no collusion."

problem: Not every removal poll runs under the 2:1 norm: SD-4 expects a design change after a successful final ballot to have near-unanimous consent (f:near-unanimous), and judges changes at ballot comment resolution by whether they improve consensus. Failed removal polls with more Favor than Against votes then mix polls under different tests, so their share does not measure the 2:1 hurdle alone.
fix: Limit the comparison to removal polls outside ballot comment resolution: "Of those, a removal poll with more Favor than Against votes but not twice as many fails ...".

problem: ISO's report reproduces every comment received but does not show which comments a national body vetted, and SD-4 notes that "some national bodies have included all comments from their members without vetting". Counting ballot comments as stated positions therefore overstates them by an amount the evidence cannot show, which weakens both the prediction and "positions on most would count against it" in c:pred-nb-positions.
fix: Treat each body's ballot comments as an upper bound on its stated positions, and count as positions only comments the body says it vetted.

problem: A body whose experts attend in person also has experts who took part in the subgroup discussions and saw some of their views lose, so it has more to disagree with as well as a cheaper way to form positions. The rival explanation, agreement, then also predicts more positions from such bodies, so "agreement predicts no such difference" is unsupported.
fix: Hold engagement fixed: compare the same body's positions at meetings its experts attend in person with those at meetings they follow remotely.

problem: "Each choice the Theorem leaves open is made the way that does best for its player given the others' choices" assumes what needs showing: that the open choices, such as the convenor's open calls, a design room chair's one-meeting delay, a result-seeking author's vehicle request, and each participant's study, admit a set of mutual best responses. A game need not have a settled pattern in which each player makes one fixed choice, and nothing here shows these choices have one, so "the choices form a settled pattern" is unsupported.
fix: State it as a premise: "Given choices left open that form a settled pattern among themselves, the named choices complete a settled pattern," which holds because each named choice does best whatever the others choose.

problem: The basis cites f:remote, but the sentence omits that ISO asks for remote participation at face-to-face meetings "to the extent possible", which lowers the cost of taking part for those who cannot travel. SD-4 gives subgroup votes to "each person in the room" (f:one-vote) without saying whether a remote participant is in the room, and that decides whether l:settled-user's "full price" is the price of a vote.
fix: State the remote-participation clause here, and state once whether the proof counts a remote participant as in the room under f:one-vote.

problem: "A small proposal's author is also a result-seeking or design-bound author, or both" does not follow from the definitions. ax:prefer lets any participant value adoption of the proposals they support and their standing, so an author can gain from adoption in any form, neither from how well the design serves users nor from fixed features. m:players lists only the two types, so the Theorem says nothing about such an author's choices.
fix: State the scope once in m:players: "The proof treats every author as result-seeking, design-bound, or valuing both, and an author who values adoption alone is outside the pattern," and cite that scope here in place of "is also".

problem: "SD-4 asks no paper to state those needs, so a design-bound author does best proposing first the smallest part" draws the wrong inference. The missing request explains why the author can leave out what later parts need; the reason the smallest part is best comes from l:first-part-smallest, that it is ready and reviewed sooner.
fix: Write "SD-4 asks no paper to state those needs, and the smallest such part is ready and reviewed soonest, so a design-bound author does best proposing it first," citing l:first-part-smallest.

problem: When the larger of the two first parts is the whole design, choosing the smaller adds at least one later part with its own paper, presenter, and polls, costs l:part-cost lists. The lemma weighs only how soon the features are fixed, so "does better with the smaller" is unsupported where those added costs exceed the gain from fixing the features sooner.
fix: Add the condition "when fixing them sooner outweighs the paper, presentation, and polls any added part takes," citing l:part-cost, and give p:first-part and the Theorem the same condition.

problem: "Others cannot study that in detail until those parts are presented" fails when the later parts are already published, in a paper in the mailings or a public implementation, since any reviewer can then read what they will need before they are presented. ax:first-review states the same limit without that exception, while c:pred-first-part relies on later parts that "already exist in drafts, implementations, or talks". p:first-part and l:thm-first-part inherit the gap.
fix: Narrow the subject: "Others cannot study in detail what unpublished later parts will need until those parts are presented," and give ax:first-review and l:thm-first-part the same scope.

problem: An author cannot know beforehand that a poll "can pass", and a failed direction poll has a lasting cost: SD-4 lets anyone ask the chair not to spend extended time on a proposal "in a direction that previously did not get interest or consensus" (f:private-concern). Seeking polls as early as possible raises that risk, which the lemma does not weigh, so it holds only when the outcome is known.
fix: Write "as early as it expects them to pass, weighing that a failed poll lets a direction count as one that did not get consensus," citing f:private-concern and f:timebox.

problem: "which is all that author's gain depends on" goes beyond d:design-bound, which says a design-bound author's gain depends on fixed features, not that nothing else adds to it. A sponsor's interests can also gain from the early implementers and users a TS brings (f:ts-unblock), so l:bound-vehicle's choice of the IS is unsupported for such an author.
fix: Either write d:design-bound as "depends only on the adopted design keeping ..." or write here "leaves those features no more fixed, which is the part of that author's gain a TS affects", and make l:bound-vehicle conditional on early reach being worth less to the author than the TS's delay and risk.

problem: "stating the trade-off costs no adoption, and with other values held equal the author ranks it first" holds time equal, but stating it takes time to write (inf:seeking-costs, ax:review-cost), so the two options differ in a value ax:prefer names. The table's case does not say the better design outweighs that time.
fix: Add to the t:disclose caption "Writing the statement takes time worth less to a result-seeking author than the change it brings," and cite it here.

problem: SD-4's alternatives item continues, in text the proof does not quote: "The author should demonstrate that they have considered the problem reasonably thoroughly, and are not just running with the first idea that occurred to them." It sets no duty to list drawbacks, but it is a check on leaving out a known trade-off, and inf:omit-free and the Theorem's disclosure claims omit it.
fix: Add the sentence to f:show-alternatives and write "SD-4 asks a good paper to show the alternatives considered and that its author considered the problem reasonably thoroughly, but asks no paper to state its design's drawbacks."

problem: For a design shipped in a TS or white paper, SD-4 puts implementers and users "on notice to expect breaking changes (they typically should not rely on the feature in production code)" (f:ts-feedback), and adds, in text the proof does not quote, "WG21 has never adopted a TS or white paper into the IS without significant change." Less is built on such a design outside WG21, and change is expected, so its reversal cost grows more slowly, which bears on the Theorem's claim that content is fixed early.
fix: Add the unquoted sentence as a Fact, and state that for a design in a TS or white paper, the work built outside WG21 is work SD-4 tells implementers and users to expect to change.

problem: Beside the TS merge default, SD-4 calls the TS lag "a limited 'grace period' wherein any participants who prefer a different approach than the one in that proposal should be actively working on developing their own alternative proposals." The proof does not quote it, though it is the rules' call for the actively progressing alternatives that switch the default off.
fix: Add a Fact quoting the grace-period sentence and cite it beside f:ts-default here and in l:ts-merge-default.

problem: The prediction turns on how many of those present at each poll one sponsor pays, but who was in the room appears only in meeting records SD-4 password-protects (f:protected), and quotable results give counts only. inf:sa-evidence covers who pays but not who was present, so "the more of those present it pays" has no public evidence.
fix: Restate the prediction with the share of the proposal's authors one sponsor pays, which author lists show, or state that the count present needs consent or protected records.

problem: "A longer revision takes more time to read" holds for a first reader, but a participant who studied the previous revision reads mainly what changed, and SD-4 expects a revision for each meeting (f:direction-implement). For the returning readers likeliest to vote, the extra reading is the added length, so the fall in votes c:pred-abstention-length predicts from total length is overstated.
fix: Measure growth as the length added since the previous revision.

problem: A first paper can leave out what later parts need because those parts were not yet designed when it appeared, and then the omission favors neither explanation. "first papers leaving it out favor the model, whoever wrote them" counts those papers anyway.
fix: Limit it as inf:fp-tell-apart does: "first papers leaving out later parts that already existed when they appeared favor the model."

problem: The prediction is "for design-bound authors", but the rules ask no author to state what their gain depends on (f:no-interest-statement), so the mailings cannot show which first papers design-bound authors wrote, and "Finding no such omissions would count against it" has no sample to apply to.
fix: Name an observable stand-in, such as first papers whose authors' stated sponsor has a product that depends on the design's features, or predict the omissions among all first papers with more of them from that stand-in group.

problem: Self-funding and its loss cannot be read from the mailings: the rules ask no author to state who pays their costs (f:no-interest-statement), and a stated affiliation can be an employer that does not pay for WG21 work. inf:sf-tell-apart treats a change of stated affiliation as the loss of a sponsor.
fix: State that a stated affiliation stands in for who pays, and count as direct evidence only cases where the paper or author states who pays.

problem: The prediction follows from its own condition with little else: if some unresolved objections point to real defects, features forwarded over them keep those defects (inf:de-kept). No difference then fails to count against the model, since it also follows when the condition fails, and a difference supports p:least-cost-response more than the settled pattern as a whole.
fix: Write "No difference would count against the condition or against p:least-cost-response," and state that the corollary tests inf:de-kept given the condition.

problem: Topics that draw competing papers are often the harder ones, with more parts and interactions, which ax:unknown ties to more unnoticed defects. Matching only implementation experience and turnout leaves that difference in place, and it works against the prediction, so "No difference would count against the prediction" in inf:co-predict is unsupported.
fix: Match also on scope and size, as inf:de-tell-apart does.

problem: Proposals whose authors come from separate sponsors draw on more organizations' interests, so their margins can differ from single-sponsor proposals before any limit, and the comparison under the limit mixes that difference with the limit's effect.
fix: Predict a change: "after the limit starts, margins for proposals whose authors one sponsor pays beyond it fall relative to margins for proposals with as many authors paid by separate sponsors."

problem: If the required record is the minutes, which stay out of public quotation, stating the objection in the paper still puts it in a public document that lasts for decades, the cost p:written-answer names. "Leaving the objection out of the paper then saves the author little" holds only when the required record is public.
fix: Narrow the lever in c:lever-written-answer to "a written answer to each objection in a public record", or state that the prediction assumes a public record.

problem: Without the delay, a TS would still need a formal ballot whose comments "must be formally responded to with a Disposition of Comments paper", and ISO editing (f:ts-disposition), so "the cost left to an author of accepting one would be the risk that experience brings incompatible changes first" is false for a TS. A white paper avoids most of that (f:white-paper-process).
fix: Write "the cost left would be the risk that experience brings incompatible changes first and, for a TS, its ballot, Disposition of Comments, and ISO editing, which a white paper avoids."

problem: "Whatever the others choose" includes the chair's choice of poll, and SD-4 lets a chair take any polls they choose (f:chair-polls), including one asking the room to prefer one colleague's design over another's. In such a poll a Favor vote for one colleague's proposal is an Against vote on the other colleague's, which ax:support says can cost that colleague's support, so Favor does not cost the regular "no standing" and need not do best. l:settled-regular and the Theorem's "A regular votes Favor on colleagues' proposals they support" rest on this lemma.
fix: A scope stated once, in l:settled-regular: the regular's votes are on polls whose Favor and Against concern one proposal, as each of SD-4's multiple polls does (f:multiple-polls); in a poll between two colleagues' designs, Favor on one counts as Against the other and bears ax:support's cost.

problem: A direction poll asks whether to continue work on a design (d:polls), so one that fails is a decision against continuing, and SD-4 lets a chair time-box a later new proposal "in a direction that previously did not get interest or consensus" (f:private-concern, f:timebox). The author cannot know in advance which poll will pass, yet the lemma weighs only the gain of passing sooner (inf:early-incumbent, inf:early-protects), not the cost of failing sooner, and the Theorem's sentence on early direction polls inherits the gap.
fix: Narrow the subject: "A design-bound author does best seeking direction polls as early as it expects them to pass, once it weighs that a failed direction poll is a decision against continuing work on the design."

problem: "which is all that author's gain depends on" goes beyond d:design-bound, which says the gain depends on particular features staying fixed, not that it depends on nothing else. A sponsor whose interests include implementing a design early, or users relying on it early, gains from a TS's earlier reach to implementers and users (f:ts-unblock), and ax:prefer has its participants value those interests. l:bound-vehicle's "does best asking the design room for the IS" and the Theorem's "asks for the IS" are then unsupported for such an author.
fix: Narrow the subject: "For a design-bound author whose gain depends only on the adopted design keeping those features, a TS's earlier reach adds nothing", and state that scope once in l:bound-vehicle and the Theorem.

problem: A proposal's authors are participants who vote Favor on it (inf:sl-predict), so a proposal with more authors paid by one sponsor shows a smaller Against share of the Favor-plus-Against votes even if no other paid participant weighs their doubt differently. The predicted smaller share then follows from the author count alone, and finding it would not support inf:sa-fewer-against, the step the corollary tests.
fix: Narrow the subject: predict the smaller Against share after setting aside the authors' own Favor votes, which the paper's author list bounds, or compare proposals with the same number of authors that differ in how many other participants their sponsor pays.

problem: After a move a participant hears the new colleagues' technical arguments, and ax:attention says what a participant learns from discussion can change their vote. A turn toward Against that starts only after the move therefore fits learning from new colleagues as well as the new sponsor's interests, so the timing test does not tell the model apart from the technical-views explanation c:pred-sponsor-against names.
fix: Narrow the test: the new sponsor's interests apply from the move, so the model predicts the turn at the first polls after it, while learning predicts a turn that grows with time among new colleagues; a turn at once that does not grow favors the model.

problem: The prediction covers first papers by design-bound authors, but the rules ask no author to state what their gain depends on (f:no-interest-statement, p:same-moves), so the mailings do not show which first papers are theirs. Without a stated way to pick those papers, "Finding no such omissions would count against it" cannot be checked, and omissions found among all first papers belong to c:pred-parts's test, not this one.
fix: Add a stated proxy: first papers whose authors' stated affiliation ties them to a sponsor whose interests depend on the design's features, as inf:sa-evidence allows, and predict more omissions there than among other first papers.

problem: SD-4 asks every participant to "Accept group decisions" (f:accept-decisions) and describes continued objection after a consensus call, without new information, as not accepting one (p:repeat-objection). That norm also predicts a like rival losing support right after a direction poll with the incumbent's content and review time unchanged, since backing the rival then continues an objection the room decided, so the comparison does not tell the reversal's cost apart from the norm.
fix: Narrow the test: the model predicts a loss that grows with the work built on the incumbent after the poll (p:challenger-bar, ind:reversal-grows), while the norm predicts one drop at the poll, so compare rival polls at different amounts of work built since the direction poll.

problem: The test needs each subgroup chair's plenary answer, but no item says it is public. SD-4 keeps meeting discussion notes on the meeting wikis (SD-4, "Purpose and audience"), password-protects meeting wikis, and lets words attributed to a specific person be quoted publicly only with that person's prior consent (f:protected). The data that tells the two explanations apart may then be unusable without each chair's consent, a limit inf:sa-consent states for its own test.
fix: Add the cited facts and the condition, as inf:sa-consent does: "Where those answers are kept in meeting wikis, using them publicly needs each chair's prior consent (f:protected)."

problem: Within one proposal, length grows with revision order, so any reason votes fall as a proposal ages produces the same pattern; for example, participants who studied an earlier revision closely and settled their view can skip later polls, which f:not-vote allows. Holding the topic fixed sets aside narrowness but not revision order, so a fall would not favor the model over aging.
fix: Narrow the test: compare revisions at the same place in their proposals' sequences, such as second revisions that grew much against second revisions that grew little, each relative to other papers polled at the same meetings.

problem: An author cannot state what later parts will need of the first if those parts are not yet designed when the first paper appears, so first papers leaving it out fit an evolving design as well as the model. c:pred-first-part restricts its test to later parts that already existed (inf:fp-small-steps, inf:fp-tell-apart), but this step counts every omission, "whoever wrote them".
fix: Narrow the subject: "first papers leaving out what later parts already existing in drafts, implementations, or talks will need of them favor the model", matching inf:fp-tell-apart.

problem: The step weighs only the costs of a written answer (inf:wa-cost), but p:written-answer gives the author a gain as well: an answer stating the objection shows later readers what a repeated objection must add, SD-4's test for new information (f:ballot-new-info). Nothing shows the costs outweigh that gain for most authors whose papers advance over Against votes, so "often leave unstated" is unsupported.
fix: Add the premise that, for most such authors, the time to write an answer and the easier raising again outweigh what the answer shows later readers, and cite p:written-answer in the step.

problem: Participants who voted Against a feature have more reason than others to test it after adoption, since new information can reopen a decided matter (f:ballot-new-info, f:late-info). Features forwarded over Against votes then draw more search for defects after adoption even when no objection pointed to a real defect, and matching on scope, novelty, implementation, use, and votes cast leaves that search unheld, so a remaining difference can favor the model without the mechanism c:pred-defects tests.
fix: Narrow the test: count only defects found after adoption that match what an objection named before the forwarding poll, as the published papers raising the objections show.

problem: "Objections count only in fixed forms and at fixed times" reads as saying an objection matters only through those forms. SD-4 asks anyone with a concern to raise it as early as possible, in discussion or before a meeting on a reflector (f:report-early), and what a participant learns from discussion can change their vote (ax:attention), so an objection can change a count whenever it persuades. What l:objection-forms proves is narrower, and the Theorem repeats the broad wording.
fix: Narrow the subject to what l:objection-forms proves: "An objection counts in a subgroup poll only as a vote cast in the room, and at plenary only if escalated by the deadline", here and in the Theorem.

problem: The lemma says each choice the Theorem leaves open "is made the way that does best for its player given the others' choices", but no item shows such choices exist together. The open choices depend on one another, for example whether a participant studies a paper can depend on what others' study will find, and the convenor's open call depends on the votes cast, so choices, one per player, that each do best given the rest need not exist. "So the choices form a settled pattern" is then unproved.
fix: Add the premise that the choices left open admit choices, one per player, each doing best given the others, or state the result as: with any such choices in what the Theorem leaves open, the named choices complete a settled pattern.

problem: The small author's best choice rests on bearing each meeting's cost alone (l:small-wait-cost), and "alone" uses both of d:small's attributes, one author and paying their own costs. With two self-funded authors either can present at a meeting, so each can bear less of the meetings still ahead; "rests only on paying their own costs" drops the one-author attribute, and l:thm-sizes, the Theorem's last sentence, and c:pred-small-fade's "self-funded authors' proposals" inherit this.
fix: Narrow the subject: "its author's best choice rests on being the only author and paying their own costs, so it holds for any proposal with one self-funded author".

problem: Every participant is an expert a national body or liaison appoints and registers (f:experts-appointed, f:registered, inf:user-joins), so how many of one sponsor's employees vote in a room depends on whom national bodies appoint, a check the proposition omits while naming only SC22's power to cap appointments. National bodies are players, yet l:settled-nb weighs only their ballot votes and timing, so the settled pattern says nothing of how they use appointment, and l:settled-sponsor and the Theorem's "no rule limits how many voters one sponsor pays for" leave this check out.
fix: Add the cited fact to the sentence: "each participant a sponsor pays must be appointed by a national body or liaison, which chooses whom it appoints"; list those appointments among the checks in p:checks, and take national bodies' appointment choices as given in m:players.

problem: A national body's own rules can give users a vote on its position. INCITS gives one voting membership to each organization, which includes self-employed or self-financed individuals (f:incits-one-vote, f:incits-organization), and its Executive Board receives voting recommendations from its technical committees when it sets the United States position (f:incits-position; INCITS Organization, Policies and Procedures, 8.2). A user who never attends WG21 can thus vote where that position is formed, so "No user votes" and "the needs that reach a vote are those participants and their sponsors know" hold only for WG21's polls and the ballot votes themselves, and l:settled-user lists no such move.
fix: A scope stated once: "vote" here means a vote in WG21's polls or a national body's ballot; add that a national body's own rules can give users a vote on its position, as INCITS's do for self-financed individuals, and add that move to m:moves-user and l:settled-user.

problem: A removal a national body requests in a ballot comment is decided in ballot comment resolution, where SD-4 says "Any technical changes made during ballot comment resolution have one goal: to improve consensus." (SD-4, "Ballots and comments"), and ISO says "Every attempt shall be made to resolve negative votes." (f:respond-comments). Those rules give a chair a stated reason beyond the room's count to accept a removal that answers a negative vote, so "needs the 2:1 norm in a design room" overstates the burden on the ballot-comment route, and p:burden-flip, p:late-arrival, and c:pred-removals inherit it.
fix: Add the cited SD-4 sentence and a scope: the 2:1 burden covers removal by paper outside ballot comment resolution, while a removal answering a national body's negative vote is weighed toward improving consensus.

problem: "negative votes without technical comments go uncounted" omits ISO's step for them: "In the case where a National Body has voted negatively and has submitted technical comments that are not clearly of a technical nature, the Secretary/Committee Manager shall contact the National Body within two weeks of the ballot closure. If the committee leadership and the National Body do not find an agreement, the matter is escalated to the technical management board via the Office of the CEO." (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 2.6.2; 2.7.2 says the same of final drafts). A national body's No leaves the count only after that contact and any escalation.
fix: Add the cited fact and narrow the wording: "negative votes found, after that step, to have no comments of a technical nature go uncounted".

problem: ISO limits positions on a document under ballot: "When a document is out for ballot or for commenting at the committee stage, formal discussion during official meetings or distribution of positions using official ISO and IEC IT tools is prohibited." (ISO/IEC Directives Part 1, 1.7.5). Cheaper national positions during meetings cannot reach the sections of a draft that is out for ballot or comment, a check the corollary does not state.
fix: Add the cited fact and a scope: the predicted effect covers proposals and sections not in a document out for ballot or comment.

problem: Work continues during an appeal only "up to and including the approval stage" (f:appeal-continues), so an upheld appeal can still stop a draft before publication, and a national body can also escalate in SC22 and JTC 1 an objection to a WG meeting that acted on a topic not on its agenda (f:agenda-notice). The ballot vote is then not the only move that counts directly toward stopping a document, and inf:nl-predict's "fewer checks" rests on this step.
fix: Narrow the wording: "the ballot vote is the only such move open on any ground", since an appeal on a draft needs a question of principle or harm to ISO's or IEC's reputation (f:appeal-technical) and an agenda objection needs off-agenda action.

problem: SD-4 calls out of harmony a ballot comment repeating an objection decided with its national body present and heard, unless it brings new information or a long-warned No (f:ballot-decided, f:ballot-new-info, f:no-surprise), and out of scope one asking for a new feature (f:ballot-no-new-features). The rules themselves thus keep vetted ballot comments off most proposals whatever positions a body forms, so counting them cannot show "positions on most", the evidence c:pred-nb-positions says would count against it.
fix: Add those cited facts and narrow the evidence to comments on matters the rules leave open to a ballot comment: items not decided with the body present, or new information.
